study type: retrospective chart analysis and telephone survey
cohort: The study included 29 patients with FIGO stage IA2-IB2 cervical cancer treated with radical abdominal trachelectomy between 2013 and 2022 at an Austrian tertiary care center.
finding: Radical abdominal trachelectomy appears oncologically safe in early-stage cervical cancers that do not meet the "low-risk" criteria, with no recurrences observed and a 62.5% live birth rate among those attempting to conceive.
